question: True or false: Albert Einstein called compound interest the most powerful force in the universe.
answer: False, as far as anyone can find. Nothing Einstein wrote or said contains it; the attribution appears decades after his death. Quote Investigator traced praise of compounding's power to a 1916 bank advertisement. The maths needs no famous name: at 7% a year, money doubles about every ten years.
move: Judge a claim by its arithmetic, not by the name attached to it.
ask: Which quote have I believed mainly because of the famous name under it?
trap: Trusting a quote because it is famous and sounds right.
source: Quote Investigator, on compound interest and Einstein, 2011
